Definition: from G3985; a putting to proof (by experiment (of good), experience (of evil), solicitation, discipline or provocation); by implication, adversity:--temptation, X try.
BiblicalUsage: Peirasmos is temptation, a putting to the proof. Jesus taught us to pray, “Lead us not into temptation,” and on the night of His arrest He told the disciples to pray that they enter not into temptation. Paul promises God will not suffer us to be tempted above what we are able, but will make a way of escape, and James blesses the man who endures temptation, for he shall receive the crown of life.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that temptation is not a sign God has left me; it is the place where His faithfulness is proved. He measures the trial to my strength and opens the way out before I need it. I hold that enduring is itself the victory — the crown is promised not to the man who never faced temptation but to the man who stood in it. And prayer is the first weapon: Jesus told His friends to pray, and they slept instead.
